hooks.prompt:
Claude's final reply (last_assistant_message in the hook input below) is clear to the user on one read and makes plain what the user needs to do.

The condition is SATISFIED straight away if either is true:
- stop_hook_active is true (the reply was already revised once).
- The reply is a single question, or one or two plain sentences with no file names, IDs or settings keys.

Otherwise the condition is NOT satisfied if ANY of these tests fails:
a) Outcome first. The opening sentence says in plain words the answer, or what is now different for the user. "Done.", "Fixed.", a version number or a file name alone is not an outcome.
b) Enumerated. Applies only when the reply covers more than one topic or runs past five sentences. After the opening sentence, the content is a numbered list. Each item has at most two sentences of content, then ends with a one-sentence recommendation. A short label at the start of an item does not count as a sentence.
c) Actions explicit. Every decision or task for the user is a direct question or instruction, and the reader can tell at a glance which items need the user and which need nothing.
d) No unexplained identifiers. Three or more internal identifiers (file or script names, version strings, tool or function IDs, rule numbers, page or commit IDs, config keys, code values like True or False) that are not each described in plain words fail this test.
e) No padding. It does not repeat itself or use empty closers like "all set" in place of saying what changed.
Ordinary technical words (script, repo, hook, Notion, commit, plugin) are fine and are not identifiers.

When the condition is NOT satisfied, the reason must name the failed test or tests, give the single most important fix, and tell Claude to restate the reply shorter in that shape: outcome sentence, then (when test b applies) numbered items of two sentences plus a one-sentence recommendation.

Hook input (JSON): $ARGUMENTS
